newsitem.title: UK: British Gas shares gain after FT report.
newsitem.headline: British Gas shares gain after FT report.

text.p: Shares in British Gas Plc bounced higher on Thursday after a report in the Financial Times said major investment institutions were seriously underweight in the stock, traders said
The stock was up 8p at 226-1/2 by 1121 GMT in heavy trading of 7.3 million shares, making it the third most active stock in the UK market.
"It's follow-up from the FT story," said one trader.
The FT said data from Citywatch, an equity ownership research group, showed Mercury Asset Management and other major institutions had big underweight positions in British Gas.

It also quoted an analyst saying the company's recent agreement on the capping of costly take-or-pay contracts gave funds a reason to reconsider their positions in the stock, which underperformed the market through much of 1995 and 1996.
British Gas is also in the throes of a demerger intended to separate its transportation network and its oil and gas exploration activities from its gas sales and trading business.

"We have had the demerger proposals and having been a very very poor performer we have seen some recovery," said another trader. "It is the end of the year and people are looking around for shares that are undervalued as they take positions for 1997."
